title: Làm ơn đừng chụp ảnh tôi
englishTitle: Please do not take my photo
pronunciation: Lam on dung chup anh toi
summary: For politely setting a photo boundary without turning the exchange into an argument.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use it once, clearly, when a camera or phone is pointed at you.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Keep your voice calm and your hand gesture small. The line is direct enough without extra explanation.

phrases.vietnamese: Làm ơn đừng chụp ảnh tôi
phrases.english: Please do not take my photo
phrases.pronunciation: Lam on dung chup anh toi

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Làm ơn means please; đừng chụp ảnh means do not take photos; tôi means me.

breakdown.vietnamese: Làm ơn đừng chụp ảnh tôi
breakdown.english: Please do not take my photo

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: Photography-allowed, photo-here, and what-to-avoid phrases cover the nearby photo-rule context.

phrases.vietnamese: Có được phép chụp ảnh không?
phrases.pronunciation: Co duoc phep chup anh khong

phrases.vietnamese: Tôi có thể chụp ảnh ở đây được không?
phrases.english: Can I take a photo here?
phrases.pronunciation: Toi co the chup anh o day duoc khong

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Good in markets, homestays, tours, cafes, and street moments when you do not want to be photographed.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: A short no is kinder than a long apology. Smile if it feels right, then move on.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: No-thank-you, alone-thank-you, not-interested, excuse-me, and thank-you-for-understanding phrases cover the boundary after that.

phrases.vietnamese: Tôi muốn ở một mình, cảm ơn bạn
